items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: the same harmonic structure that you were learning in your music appreciation course from Bach

ctx.x: But at Hamilton we never heard of bebop. We were up there. We were up on that hill up there. Who knew from bebop? So number one, up until the late forties there really wasn’t a lot of awareness of bebop except in very, very, like people, kids who were living in New York City and could get to 52nd Street occasionally and hear it. So there was not that much awareness. In the second place, when you did hear it you heard Bird and Diz playing at those high tempos and playing these funny changes. I mean you just right…
